title: Overzealous Consistency / Design Pattern Abuse
pattern: Applying heavy design patterns (like Strategy, Abstract Factory, or Decorator) to simple operations solely to make them consistent with other complex structures.
why_bad: It focuses on consistency of form over functionality, inflating file count, boilerplate, and indirection. It increases the difficulty of understanding simple tasks without providing any technical value.
detection: An implementation of a complex behavioral design pattern (like Strategy or State) wrapping a trivial, immutable operation (like returning a static string literal) with zero active runtime variation.
counterexample: Complex polymorphic behavior where actual dynamic runtime selection is strictly required by business needs. Mark the rule `Context-dependent`.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 17.3: "Taking it too far", p. 116, 512; Sandi Metz *POODR*, Chapter 1: "Pattern Abuse", p. 192.
